summary: The day lends itself to one SQL task, a CREATE VIEW over the desk's tables whose column names, rows and live link to the tickets table a SELECT can read back in sqlite3; triggers, procedures, functions and EXPLAIN are MySQL syntax or MySQL behaviour that SQLite 3.39 does not run unchanged, and the review is a recap with connector, Docker and pytest code.

steps.title: Triggers: SQL that runs when a row changes
steps.reason: Triggers are on the critic's list of steps that stay none until ix-sql lands: the page's trigger needs DELIMITER, an IF block, the NULL-safe <=> and CONCAT, none of which SQLite runs unchanged. A lone SELECT on NULL <=> NULL would also fail on SQLite and would practise an operator, not the trigger the step teaches.

steps.title: Views: a saved query with a name
steps.reason: CREATE VIEW over a join with aliases runs unchanged on SQLite 3.39 and MySQL 9.7, and a SELECT from the view shows its column names and rows, so the page's points become checks: aliases name the view's columns, a NULL test needs IS NULL, and a view holds no rows of its own and follows the table. The task stays off open_board (the walkthrough's view, which uses CONCAT and DATE_ADD) and the exercise's library overdue_loans.

steps.title: Stored procedures: a unit of work kept in the database
steps.reason: Stored procedures, CALL, IN and OUT parameters, DELIMITER and callproc are on the critic's list of steps that stay none until ix-sql lands: SQLite has no CREATE PROCEDURE, so no statement of this step runs in the page's sqlite3.

steps.title: User-defined functions: one value, used inside a query
steps.reason: Stored functions are on the critic's list of steps that stay none until ix-sql lands: SQLite has no CREATE FUNCTION, and the step's mistakes (a missing DETERMINISTIC refused with error 1418, NULL from TIMESTAMPDIFF) are MySQL behaviour SQLite cannot show.

steps.title: Indexes: finding rows without reading them all
steps.reason: The step's evidence is the EXPLAIN plan reading Table scan or Index lookup, and EXPLAIN is on the critic's list of steps that stay none. A CREATE INDEX changes no rows a SELECT returns, so a check could only read SQLite's own catalog, which the page never teaches, and the exercise already checks idx_loans_due_on and its plan.

steps.title: Review: the week's desk in one database
steps.reason: The review recaps the week and the choice between trigger, view, procedure, function and index, a judgement the Check yourself questions practise. Its code is a placeholder query through mysql-connector-python, a docker exec rebuild and a pytest fixture, none of which is one SQL statement the page's sqlite3 can run.

tasks.title: Views
tasks.idea: The reader writes one CREATE VIEW statement for unassigned_queue: the tickets with status 'open' and no agent, joined to customers, with the columns ticket_id, title, priority and customer (the customer's name under that alias), ordered by ticket_id. On the page's six tickets plus ticket 7 'Reset link expired' (normal, Omar Haddad, open, no agent, as step 0 inserts it), SELECT * FROM unassigned_queue returns (6, 'Add dark mode', 'low', 'Mei Chen') and (7, 'Reset link expired', 'normal', 'Omar Haddad'), and assigning ticket 6 an agent with an UPDATE drops it from the next read.
checks: SELECT * FROM unassigned_queue has the columns ticket_id, title, priority, customer in that order; leaving out AS customer names the last column name instead.

The view returns exactly the open tickets with no agent, in ticket_id order; writing agent_id = NULL in place of agent_id IS NULL returns no rows, and dropping the status test lets a closed ticket through.
After an UPDATE gives ticket 6 an agent, a second SELECT from the view no longer returns it; a CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT copy keeps the old row, because only a view runs its query on every read.
tasks.q: Write one CREATE VIEW statement, inside the quotes of QUERY, that makes a view named unassigned_queue: the tickets whose status is 'open' and whose agent_id is NULL, joined to customers on customer_id. The view's columns are ticket_id, title, priority and customer (the customer's name under that alias), in that order, and its rows come in ticket_id order. The checks build the desk's priorities, customers, agents and tickets tables with closed, assigned and open tickets, ticket 7 'Reset link expired' among them (normal, Omar Haddad, open, no agent). On those rows SELECT * FROM unassigned_queue returns (6, 'Add dark mode', 'low', 'Mei Chen') and (7, 'Reset link expired', 'normal', 'Omar Haddad'). After UPDATE tickets SET agent_id = 3 WHERE ticket_id = 6, the next read of the view returns ticket 7 alone.
tasks.starter:
QUERY = """
-- a view of the open tickets with no agent, with each customer's name
"""
tasks.tests:
import sqlite3
conn = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
conn.executescript("""
CREATE TABLE priorities (priority VARCHAR(10) PRIMARY KEY, sla_hours INT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE customers (customer_id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE agents (agent_id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE tickets (
    ticket_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    title VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    priority VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL REFERENCES priorities (priority),
    status VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open' CHECK (status IN ('open', 'assigned', 'closed')),
    customer_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES customers (customer_id),
    agent_id INT REFERENCES agents (agent_id)
);
INSERT INTO priorities VALUES ('high', 4), ('normal', 24), ('low', 72);
INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1, 'Dana Whitfield'), (2, 'Ravi Patel'), (3, 'Mei Chen'), (4, 'Omar Haddad');
INSERT INTO agents VALUES (1, 'Priya'), (2, 'Marco'), (3, 'Sam');
INSERT INTO tickets VALUES
    (1, 'Login page returns 500', 'high', 'closed', 1, NULL),
    (2, 'Invoice PDF is blank', 'normal', 'closed', 2, NULL),
    (4, 'Checkout button frozen', 'high', 'assigned', 3, 1),
    (5, 'Export is missing rows', 'normal', 'assigned', 2, 2),
    (6, 'Add dark mode', 'low', 'open', 3, NULL),
    (7, 'Reset link expired', 'normal', 'open', 4, NULL);
""")
conn.execute(QUERY)
cur = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM unassigned_queue")
rows = cur.fetchall()
assert [c[0] for c in cur.description] == ["ticket_id", "title", "priority", "customer"], "the view's columns are ticket_id, title, priority and customer, in that order"
assert rows == [(6, "Add dark mode", "low", "Mei Chen"), (7, "Reset link expired", "normal", "Omar Haddad")], "the view returns the open tickets with no agent, one row each, in ticket_id order"
conn.execute("UPDATE tickets SET agent_id = 3 WHERE ticket_id = 6")
assert conn.execute("SELECT * FROM unassigned_queue").fetchall() == [(7, "Reset link expired", "normal", "Omar Haddad")], "after ticket 6 gets an agent, the next read of the view leaves it out"
